clue.text: Call notes of an uncertain nature

parts.note: to dub is to call or name someone
IOUs are written promissory notes

explanation.surface: Someone's phone call left notes of doubtful character.
explanation.definitionFit: Something doubtful or questionable is of an uncertain nature.

clue.text: Measure up for nest

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a yard is a unit of measure

explanation.surface: Taking measurements for a bird's nest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns YARD into the answer. A squirrel's nest is the sense needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A drey or dray is the nest a squirrel builds, a less familiar sense.

clue.text: Rehash American boy's harmony to conceal a beastly noise

parts.note: bub is American slang for a boy or man

indicators.note: the harmony word holds the article inside it, as though hiding it

parts.note: a blend is a harmonious mixture
a squeak is the noise a mouse makes

explanation.surface: An American lad's musical harmony is used to muffle an animal's cry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'harmony' suggests music, but here it means a smooth mix. BUBBLE AND SQUEAK is a British dish of fried leftover potato and cabbage.
explanation.definitionFit: The dish is made by frying up leftovers, so it is literally a rehash of an earlier meal.

clue.text: Perhaps to do better on green issue …

definitions.text: Perhaps to do better on green
definitions.meaning: to beat someone at putting on a golf green, with put as a variant spelling of putt

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether to improve on an environmental question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' reads as environmental, but it is the golf green; 'Perhaps' warns the first sense is a pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Output is what a factory or process issues, its production.

clue.text: … look at the fume

parts.note: to see something is to look at it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: just look at the fumes.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this clue to 3 down for the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: To fume and to seethe both mean to be inwardly furious.

clue.text: Where pitchers can be found for a pound

definitions.meaning: in baseball, relief pitchers warm up in a separate area beside the field
a pound is an enclosure for animals, such as a pen for a bull

explanation.surface: Somewhere jugs can be bought for a pound sterling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitchers' looks like jugs and 'pound' like money; one is baseball, the other an animal enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: The baseball warm-up area takes its name from an animal enclosure, matching both senses.

clue.text: Wager the empty colour has improved

parts.note: a bet is a wager

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its insides, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: red is a colour

explanation.surface: A bet on a colour without anything left has paid off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves TE from 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: To better something is to improve it, so bettered means improved.

clue.text: Such a child has only this present to open

definitions.text: Such a child has only this present to open

parts.words: Such a child has only this present to open
parts.note: a child who comes home to an empty house carries a door key of their own, the only thing to open

explanation.surface: A deprived child gets just one gift to unwrap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' reads as a gift, but the thing to open is the front door, which the child lets themselves in through.
explanation.definitionFit: A latchkey child lets themselves in with a door key because no parent is home.

clue.text: Supporter of images created by computer in guild

indicators.note: the letters of the following words are made into something new

explanation.surface: Pictures generated by a computer within a craft guild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter of images' sounds like a fan of pictures, but it is the rail fixed to a wall from which pictures hang.
explanation.definitionFit: A wall rail from which framed paintings are hung physically supports pictures.

clue.text: One who'll tend to guard, for example, a plant?

definitions.text: One who'll tend to guard, for example, a plant?

parts.note: to nurse is to tend to someone
a train guard is a railwayman, abbreviated RY MAN, with RY for railway

explanation.surface: A carer who looks after a plant as if it were a patient.
explanation.walkthrough: A guard here is a railway guard, giving RY (railway) and MAN; the whole clue then describes someone tending young plants.
explanation.definitionFit: A nurseryman grows and tends plants in a nursery garden.

clue.text: Big brother?

parts.note: the senior figure among monks, who call each other brother

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone is an older sibling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big brother' suggests an older sibling or Orwell's watcher; here it is the head of a community of monks.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbot is the head of an abbey, the chief among the brothers.

clue.text: Drunk at a secret saloon, perhaps

indicators.note: being drunk puts the following letters in a muddled state

explanation.surface: Someone got drunk at a hidden bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saloon' looks like a bar to drink in, but it is a type of car; 'perhaps' admits the definition is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Saloon and estate are both car body styles, so the definition is a loose example.

clue.text: Merriment disturbs quiet river, causing a shambles

indicators.note: the merriment breaks into the quiet, splitting it apart

parts.note: SH is the call for quiet
laughter is merriment
the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: Laughter breaks the peace by a river and causes chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shambles' means chaos in modern use, but its original sense is a meat market or abattoir.
explanation.definitionFit: A shambles was originally a butchers' market and so a place of slaughter.

clue.text: Decreasing to faint hint of sound?

indicators.note: the phrase tells the solver to go by how the words are spoken

parts.note: dim means faint and an innuendo is a hint

explanation.surface: Something fading to a mere whisper of sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faint hint' gives DIM INNUENDO, which spoken sounds like the musical term.
explanation.definitionFit: Diminuendo is the musical direction for a gradually decreasing volume.

clue.text: I fled country

parts.note: ran is the past tense of run, meaning fled

explanation.surface: Someone says they fled their homeland.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is a country in western Asia.

clue.text: Isle formerly cut off in a harsh way

parts.note: to sever is to cut off
Ely in Cambridgeshire was once an island in the fens, the Isle of Ely

explanation.surface: An island was once cut off in a brutal manner.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Ely was a former county area of England, a raised island in the fens before drainage.
explanation.definitionFit: Severely is an adverb for acting harshly or strictly.

clue.text: Adviser to judge fools in case at hand

annotationWithheld.why: Adviser to judge fools in case at hand (8): ASSES (fools) leaves SOR, and no reading of 'in case at hand' gives those letters soundly
annotationWithheld.clue: Adviser to judge fools in case at hand

clue.text: Puritan accepts corrupt project

indicators.note: the Puritan word takes in the other word, holding it inside

parts.note: a prude is a prim, puritanical person
to rot is to corrupt or decay

explanation.surface: A strict moralist takes on a dishonest scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'project' looks like a noun (a scheme) but is the verb, to jut out.
explanation.definitionFit: To protrude is to project or stick out.

clue.text: Go after river trade

indicators.note: the try-word is placed after the river

parts.note: the Indus is a river in Pakistan
to have a go is to try

explanation.surface: Someone goes in pursuit of river commerce.
explanation.definitionFit: Trade in the sense of a branch of commerce or manufacturing is an industry.

clue.text: Murphy's stand-in has a soft drink

parts.note: Sod's law is the British name for what Americans call Murphy's law

explanation.surface: Someone named Murphy's replacement orders a soft drink.
explanation.walkthrough: SOD'S LAW, the British saying that anything that can go wrong will, stands in for Murphy's law.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda water or a fizzy soda is a soft drink.

clue.text: It's on twig?

parts.note: the thing which, followed by the word on, means to twig or grasp an idea

explanation.surface: Asking whether something is perched on a small branch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twig' reads as a small branch, but it is slang for understand: to COTTON ON is to twig.
explanation.definitionFit: The fabric word joins on to form a phrasal verb meaning to realise or understand.

clue.text: Witch serving soldiers food

parts.note: a hag is an ugly old witch
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: A witch dishing up food to the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: HAGGIS is a Scottish dish of offal and oatmeal cooked in a sheep's stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Haggis is a savoury Scottish dish, so it is food.

clue.text: Surely search in combination with skill

indicators.note: the search word goes inside the combination word

parts.note: a union is a combination of things
a quest is a search
ably means with skill

explanation.surface: A search combined with expertise surely succeeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Surely and unquestionably both express certainty beyond doubt.

clue.text: Drink causing a lot of larks?

definitions.meaning: bevvy, spelt variously, is British slang for an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Drinking leads to plenty of fun and games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'larks' looks like fun and games, but it is the birds; 'bevy' is their collective noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A bevy is a flock or group, used especially of larks and quails.

clue.text: Unavoidably obliged to tip home counties' dustmen

indicators.note: to tip is to dump or upset, spilling the letters out into a new order

parts.note: SE, the south-east, is where the home counties lie around London

explanation.surface: Being forced to give the bin men a gratuity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip' turns SE plus DUSTMEN over. The home counties are the counties surrounding London.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom needs must means one is forced to by necessity.

clue.text: Dirt, say, swirling round edge

indicators.note: the turned letters go round the other word, enclosing it
swirling turns the word round to read the other way

parts.note: EG, for example, is what say means here
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: Dirt swirling round the edge of a sink or bath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' belongs to the wordplay, not the definition: it is the usual signal for EG, turned round by 'swirling'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: grime is a layer of sooty, ingrained filth on a surface.

clue.text: Suitable starting point to hide a monarch?

annotationWithheld.why: Suitable starting point to hide a monarch? (3,4): O(A)K + T(R)EE needs 'to hide' to signal both containers at once, one indicator doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Suitable starting point to hide a monarch?

clue.text: Feature lively little bunch

parts.note: the nose is a facial feature
gay in its older sense means lively or merry

explanation.surface: A small group with lively features.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosegay is a small bunch of flowers.
